requirements.controllingText: Repository governance MUST maintain one machine-readable closed-loop-normative-requirements/1 manifest generated from and reviewed against the controlling specification. It assigns a stable NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT_ID to every distinct normative requirement, prohibition, invariant, field contract, operation contract, negative case, regression obligation, deployment obligation, and definition-of-done metric. Each entry records the controlling text location, responsible implementation owner, schema or registry entry, deterministic and semantic test IDs, mutation-test IDs, required browser or physical-device proof, acceptance-report field, and current disposition.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Normative specification path: specification/closed-loop-reliability-controlling-implementation-specification.txt
Normative requirement manifest path: specification/closed-loop-normative-requirements.json
Verification-package schema: closed-loop-verification-package/1
Contract profile: closed-loop-completion-profile/1

The controlling normative source is the exact UTF-8 file `specification/closed-loop-reliability-controlling-implementation-specification.txt` in the exact audited source commit. CI MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-specification-manifest.json` as a repository-only closed-loop-specification-manifest/1 after reading those exact bytes and MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-normative-requirements.json` as the corresponding normative-requirement manifest. That manifest records the source commit, repository path, artifact filename, byte length, SHA-256, section inventory, contract-profile identity, and the identity and digest of the normative-requirement manifest. The manifest and source commit together identify the exact specification used for implementation and acceptance; the specification does not contain a self-referential digest of itself.

The controlling runtime contract profile is closed-loop-completion-profile/1. Runtime project state, prompts, responses, packages, imports, exports, and receipts carry only the contract profile and the particular schema or registry identities required for their own operation. The specification text, its repository-only manifest, Section 0 implementation instructions, user-to-implementation-agent instructions, audits, and repair commentary are not runtime project data and MUST NOT be embedded in the application, generated prompts, execution packages, canonical records, or operator screens merely to establish conformance.

A closed-loop-project/3 object that lacks the current contract profile is legacy /3 data. It MUST be deterministically migrated with complete migration receipts or preserved as historical and non-gating. Schema-name equality alone does not establish current contract conformance.
2.2 Normative-requirement manifest

This manifest is implementation and acceptance evidence outside runtime project state. It MUST NOT be injected into ordinary project prompts or carried by the application as project content. CI rejects missing, duplicated, untraced, or conflicting normative entries and rejects an acceptance claim when any current mandatory entry lacks the required implementation and proof relationships.

Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content. One extractor drafts the manifest from the controlling text; an independent reviewer that did not receive the draft performs its own extraction or section-by-section coverage pass; a distinct reconciliation resolves every difference; and every specification section is either covered by entries or explicitly recorded as nonnormative with a reason. CI records the challenge and reconciliation evidence with the manifest digest. An unreconciled material disagreement, an uncovered section, or a missing challenge record blocks acceptance.

The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.
The Stage 01 prompt MUST require:
Read the complete request and every accessible supplied artifact from beginning to end. Extract all distinct project-relevant human-origin statements.
Compare the extracted ledger back against every raw input unit and specifically search for omitted:
The agent MUST resolve identified omissions before returning final JSON.

Stage 03 MUST independently challenge extraction completeness when triggered by large or complex sources, uncovered source units, broad exclusions, source sections with no findings, conflicting provisions, material uncertainty, or operator request. For omission discovery, the independent extractor does not receive the first extraction until its own extraction is complete. A distinct reconciliation operation compares both outputs. Material disagreement, missing source-unit coverage, or unexamined accessible content remains BLOCKED.

Stage 04 independently challenges every proposed INAPPLICABLE disposition, every nonnormative disposition arising from language that could be normative, every classification that reduces a possible mandatory obligation, every merge of multiple obligations, every requirement with unresolved independent truth conditions, and every material uncertainty. The compiler and challenger use distinct operation reservations and external contexts. The first compiler cannot approve its own work. A distinct reconciliation operation resolves the records or leaves the affected obligation BLOCKED.
26.5 Independent semantic-review contract
Every release-bearing semantic review records:

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Additional controlling principles:
14.10 Human-origin facts first supplied during an external conversation

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 3. File-first and iPhone operating outcome
45. Browser acceptance
Browser acceptance includes:
- desktop;
- initial raw user input;
- initial file storage;
- Stage 01 exact file handoff;
- Stage 01 conversation;
- Stage 01 clarification;
- Stage 01 intent confirmation without line-by-line reconstruction review;
- Stage 01 reload persistence;
- typed human answers;
- Stage 02 canonical ingestion;
- Stage 03 complete source coverage;
- Stage 04 prompt using accepted Stage 01 and Stage 03 data;
- Stage 04 without repeated intent entry;
- multi-record response;
- pending proposal reload;
- ten-run rendering;
- upstream correction;
- downstream invalidation;
- actual Blob persistence;
- individual artifact retrieval;
- execution-package creation;
- full package export and import;
- order-independent artifact identity;
- two-tab revision conflict;
- injected storage-failure recovery;
- native Stage 22 worker execution;
- worker timeout behavior;
- no runtime exceptions;
- no horizontal overflow;
- minimum text size;
- minimum touch-target size;
- prompt preview;
- prompt collapse;
- retry behavior;
- help behavior;
- artifact handoff;
- conversation-versus-response-file state;
- contradiction warning;
- evidence explanation;
- Stage 16 root-cause correction presentation;
- prompt-box baseline dimensions;
- no unrelated visual changes.
45.1 Actual-iPhone Safari acceptance
Before final acceptance, repository governance creates one MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_TARGET_ID that freezes:
- physical-device requirement;
- iPhone model or hardware-class identity as observable;
- exact iOS version and build;
- Safari version and WebKit build identity where observable;
- viewport dimensions and device-pixel ratio;
- storage persistence and quota capability observations;
- canonical HTTPS deployment origin and base path;
- exact deployed commit, deployment-manifest digest, and running build identity;
- test-project identity and initial project package;
- operator or performer identity and identity assurance;
- acceptance procedure version;
- required screenshots, screen recording, exported receipts, logs, and project export;
- unavailable environment facts and their epistemic basis.

The required mobile acceptance executes on an actual iPhone in Safari. Simulator, desktop responsive mode, and another browser are supplementary only and cannot satisfy the physical-device requirement. "Current" is frozen by the target record; a material iOS, Safari/WebKit, application build, origin, storage behavior, or target-device change before final delivery invalidates the affected mobile result and requires revalidation.

The minimum required target-identity tuple is: the physical-device human observation; reported iOS version; observed Safari user-agent string; viewport dimensions and device-pixel ratio; exact deployed commit and deployment-manifest digest; origin; and test-project identity. WebKit build identity and exact hardware model may remain UNKNOWN without blocking; every other tuple member is required.
The actual-iPhone path must prove:
- initial project creation and raw file intake;
- prompt-file export or share without clipboard dependence;
- exact input-file attachment instructions;
- response JSON file selection and direct ingestion;
- returned-file slot selection;
- validation failure and retry recovery;
- proposal review and acceptance where required;
- canonical persistence across reload;
- artifact download/share;
- logical execution-package export;
- backup export and restore from the exported package;
- no horizontal overflow at the pinned viewport;
- required text, touch-target, focus, and live-region behavior;
- exact deployed build identity;
- no runtime exception or unhandled rejection.
A failed or incomplete physical-device result blocks final acceptance and release tagging.

Because the canonical handoff container is logical under Section 19.7, per-member sequential export or share on the pinned device satisfies package export whenever a combined multi-file share is unavailable; the optional archive representation is never required. Before the acceptance run, the acceptance procedure executes a recorded MOBILE_CAPABILITY_PROBE on the pinned target covering file export or share, response-file selection, returned-file slot selection, persistent-storage request, logical package export, and backup export and restore. A required capability the pinned target cannot perform yields BLOCKED with the exact missing capability recorded. The only permitted continuations are a new pinned target record on an iOS or Safari version that supports the capability, or a governance change to the controlling specification. No silent degradation path exists.
45.2 Physical-device evidence binding

Before the device run, CI or the authorized acceptance controller creates a cryptographically random MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE of at least 128 bits bound to the exact commit, deployment manifest, origin, target ID, procedure version, and test project. The actual iPhone loads that deployed build and the application records the challenge in its acceptance-mode receipts.

At completion, the application exports `mobile-acceptance-evidence.json` containing the target ID, challenge, build identity, origin, test-project identity, operation receipts, console/runtime findings available to the application, screenshots or recording references, exported project digest, performer identity assurance, physical-device assertion, and evidence basis. CI verifies every mechanically verifiable binding before accepting the record. The physical-device fact remains HUMAN_OBSERVATION or stronger external attestation according to the actual evidence and is never mislabeled application-proven.

The evidence file reaches CI through the repository as a committed file or authenticated workflow input from a submitter recorded in the acceptance artifact. Each MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE is single-use: CI accepts at most one evidence file per challenge and rejects reused, unknown, or expired challenges and any evidence bound to a different commit, manifest, origin, target, or test project; a superseding run requires a new challenge. The gate minimum for the physical-device fact is HUMAN_OBSERVATION by the recorded performer at the recorded identity assurance; that basis is explicitly sufficient and is never relabeled application-proven.

6.3A Authoritative Stage 01 handoff

Before accepted semantic intake, every user-supplied file is presumptively required for Stage 01 inspection unless it is mechanically empty, a byte-identical duplicate of an included file, or explicitly excluded by the human through SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT; after accepted intake, later transfer requirements follow Section 29.15 materiality.
10.1 Authoritative prompt-file identity

For every external-agent operation, the authoritative prompt is an application-generated file artifact. Its body is exactly the UTF-8 byte sequence of the exported prompt file, and promptIdentity.bodySha256 equals the application-computed SHA-256 of those exact bytes.

The current prompt-file contract is UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, no implicit line-ending conversion, no wrapper or header bytes outside the generated body, and a final newline required. Its media type is text/plain;charset=utf-8. Its canonical package path is `instruction.txt`. Its exported transport filename is <JOB_ID>_<STAGE_TWO_DIGITS>_<OPERATION>_<INSTRUCTION_ID>.txt after closed-loop-filename/1 normalization. The application preview is decoded from those authoritative bytes. Clipboard copy is optional and nonauthoritative and cannot create a second prompt identity.

The prompt file does not contain its own bodySha256 or any value whose computation depends on bodySha256. manifest.json carries promptIdentity, including the application-computed bodySha256, and the prompt instructs the external actor to echo the exact manifest promptIdentity. This avoids a self-referential prompt hash.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: - A human-origin answer stated only to an external agent remains an agent report until the application records human confirmation.
6.4A External-conversation human-answer capture

An external agent may propose that a statement originated with the human, but it cannot create or modify a HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION value. A newly reported human answer becomes authoritative only through the application confirmation path in Section 14.10. Confirmation presents the extracted answer and permits accept or correct without retyping. The application records the exact external response pointer, confirmed value, human decision receipt, and resulting input version.
14.10 Human-origin facts first supplied during an external conversation

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

requirements.controllingText: The Stage 01 accounting model MUST have two distinct layers.

atomicObligation.statement: The Stage 01 accounting model must have two distinct layers: application-owned raw-input accounting and agent-owned semantic extraction.

sourceSpans.text: The Stage 01 accounting model MUST have two distinct layers.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 6.5 Stage 01 coverage accounting
Raw-input accounting
The application owns:
- raw text-field identities;
- message or entry identities;
- artifact identities;
- file hashes;
- byte ranges, pages, paragraphs, sections, or deterministic chunks where available;
- raw-input version;
- raw-input completeness;
- whether every raw unit was included in the Stage 01 context or exact handoff.
Semantic extraction
The Stage 01 agent owns:
- extracted semantic statements;
- classification of each statement;
- source-location references;
- determination of whether information is incorporated, retained, unresolved, later-resolvable, or inapplicable;
- assumptions;
- unknowns;
- normalized deliverable description.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Stage 01 completion MUST be rejected when:

Before accepted semantic intake, every user-supplied file is presumptively required for Stage 01 inspection unless it is mechanically empty, a byte-identical duplicate of an included file, or explicitly excluded by the human through SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT; after accepted intake, later transfer requirements follow Section 29.15 materiality.

File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.

26.5 Independent semantic-review contract

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.
29.15 Normative classification, controlled exceptions, severity, and materiality

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 6.5A Raw-unitization contract

The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 7.3 Question classes
BLOCKING_NOW
- The answer must come from the human.
- The answer is required to define the Stage 01 job or deliverable.
- Stage 01 cannot complete until it is answered.
ASK_NOW_NONBLOCKING
- The answer must ultimately come from the human.
- It is foreseeable and should be asked during Stage 01.
- The human may answer "unknown" or "deferred."
- Stage 01 may complete after that explicit answer.
LATER_RESOLVABLE
- The matter can be resolved from supplied materials, authorized research, or a later stage.
- The agent must not ask the human merely because the answer is not yet known.
- The item is retained with its later resolution path.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 7.4A Human-authority provenance
14.10 Human-origin facts first supplied during an external conversation

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Before accepted semantic intake, every user-supplied file is presumptively required for Stage 01 inspection unless it is mechanically empty, a byte-identical duplicate of an included file, or explicitly excluded by the human through SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT; after accepted intake, later transfer requirements follow Section 29.15 materiality.

File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.

File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.
7.6 Stage 01 completion
Stage 01 completes only when:

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Stage 02 must permit:
- one or more legitimate inspected external authorities; or

Stage 02 MUST create one current SOURCE_SEARCH_CONTRACT defining the project and subject scope, jurisdiction or system scope where applicable, source classes considered, locations and repositories searched, queries or strategies, date or version cutoff, exclusions, access limitations, search performer and capability, execution evidence, unresolved discovery risk, and adequacy rationale. The initial search universe derives from the Stage 01 objective, known authorities, jurisdiction or system scope, a versioned source-class checklist, and every supplied reference.

DESIRED_SOURCE_COUNT is advisory only and MUST NOT cap or exclude a controlling source. Narrowing a release-bearing search universe requires explicit reasoning and an independent search-adequacy review. NO_APPLICABLE_EXTERNAL_SOURCE is permitted only after the bounded search was executed, every discovered candidate source received a disposition, the independent adequacy review accepted the procedure, and no material unresolved discovery risk remains.

The versioned source-class checklist derives from the closed generic class set — governing law and regulation; standards and specifications; controlling contracts and prior agreements; authoritative technical documentation; official registries and databases; scholarly and measurement literature; and project-supplied references — filtered by the Stage 01 objective and declared jurisdiction or system scope. Omitting an entire applicable class requires explicit reasoning and is challenged by the SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW. The contract also declares explicit stopping criteria: every registered location searched; query saturation, meaning no new candidate source in the final registered query round; authority-chain closure, meaning every authority cited by an accepted controlling source received a disposition; the declared date or version cutoff; a disposition for every inaccessible location; and the residual-risk statement. Search completion without every declared criterion is invalid.

Stage 03 researches the accepted Stage 02 sources and extracts:
26.5 Independent semantic-review contract
Every release-bearing semantic review records:
- reviewed proposal or record IDs and hashes;
- author context and operation reservation;
- reviewer context and operation reservation;
- required independence dimensions and actual bases;
- review question and allowed dispositions;
- observation and evidence IDs;
- result: ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PARTIAL, UNKNOWN, or DISAGREED;
- reconciliation requirement and status.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 8.3 Bounded source-search contract

Stage 02 MUST create one current SOURCE_SEARCH_CONTRACT defining the project and subject scope, jurisdiction or system scope where applicable, source classes considered, locations and repositories searched, queries or strategies, date or version cutoff, exclusions, access limitations, search performer and capability, execution evidence, unresolved discovery risk, and adequacy rationale. The initial search universe derives from the Stage 01 objective, known authorities, jurisdiction or system scope, a versioned source-class checklist, and every supplied reference.
26.5 Independent semantic-review contract
Every release-bearing semantic review records:
- reviewed proposal or record IDs and hashes;
- author context and operation reservation;
- reviewer context and operation reservation;
- required independence dimensions and actual bases;
- review question and allowed dispositions;
- observation and evidence IDs;
- result: ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PARTIAL, UNKNOWN, or DISAGREED;
- reconciliation requirement and status.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

The initial search universe derives from the Stage 01 objective, known authorities, jurisdiction or system scope, a versioned source-class checklist, and every supplied reference.

The versioned source-class checklist derives from the closed generic class set — governing law and regulation; standards and specifications; controlling contracts and prior agreements; authoritative technical documentation; official registries and databases; scholarly and measurement literature; and project-supplied references — filtered by the Stage 01 objective and declared jurisdiction or system scope. Omitting an entire applicable class requires explicit reasoning and is challenged by the SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW. The contract also declares explicit stopping criteria: every registered location searched; query saturation, meaning no new candidate source in the final registered query round; authority-chain closure, meaning every authority cited by an accepted controlling source received a disposition; the declared date or version cutoff; a disposition for every inaccessible location; and the residual-risk statement. Search completion without every declared criterion is invalid.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 9.6 Stage 04 semantic challenge
26.5 Independent semantic-review contract
Every release-bearing semantic review records:
- reviewed proposal or record IDs and hashes;
- author context and operation reservation;
- reviewer context and operation reservation;
- required independence dimensions and actual bases;
- review question and allowed dispositions;
- observation and evidence IDs;
- result: ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PARTIAL, UNKNOWN, or DISAGREED;
- reconciliation requirement and status.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 10.1 Authoritative prompt-file identity

The current prompt-file contract is UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, no implicit line-ending conversion, no wrapper or header bytes outside the generated body, and a final newline required. Its media type is text/plain;charset=utf-8. Its canonical package path is `instruction.txt`. Its exported transport filename is <JOB_ID>_<STAGE_TWO_DIGITS>_<OPERATION>_<INSTRUCTION_ID>.txt after closed-loop-filename/1 normalization. The application preview is decoded from those authoritative bytes. Clipboard copy is optional and nonauthoritative and cannot create a second prompt identity.

The prompt file does not contain its own bodySha256 or any value whose computation depends on bodySha256. manifest.json carries promptIdentity, including the application-computed bodySha256, and the prompt instructs the external actor to echo the exact manifest promptIdentity. This avoids a self-referential prompt hash.

19.9 Filename, format, and archive safety

Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. Canonical comparison uses Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, case-sensitive identity, and separately checked Unicode 15.1.0 default-case-fold and registered platform-risk collision keys. Absolute paths, drive prefixes, NUL, control characters, empty segments, `.` and `..`, duplicate canonical paths, case-fold collisions, extraction-target collisions, and supported confusable collisions are rejected. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.
34.1 Canonical serialization portability

NFC normalization and default case folding use Unicode 15.1.0 data. Confusable detection uses the Unicode Technical Standard #39 confusables data published for Unicode 15.1.0. These exact data identities and table digests are recorded in the runtime registry and deployment manifest. A host Unicode implementation may be used only when startup and CI conformance fixtures establish the pinned results for every supported code-point class; otherwise the application uses bundled pinned tables. An unknown host/table mismatch blocks canonical filename normalization and package activation. Runtime upgrades do not silently change canonical identities; runtime or browser Unicode behavior may not silently redefine canonical identity. Every set-valued array has one named versioned normalizer. Every contentSha256, recordSha256, project hash, package hash, proof hash, scope hash, and terminal hash has a closed JSON-pointer inclusion and omission set registered in workflow-schema.js. No implementation selects preimage fields implicitly.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 10.2 Authoritative response-file contract
19.9 Filename, format, and archive safety

Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. Canonical comparison uses Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, case-sensitive identity, and separately checked Unicode 15.1.0 default-case-fold and registered platform-risk collision keys. Absolute paths, drive prefixes, NUL, control characters, empty segments, `.` and `..`, duplicate canonical paths, case-fold collisions, extraction-target collisions, and supported confusable collisions are rejected. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.
34.1 Canonical serialization portability

NFC normalization and default case folding use Unicode 15.1.0 data. Confusable detection uses the Unicode Technical Standard #39 confusables data published for Unicode 15.1.0. These exact data identities and table digests are recorded in the runtime registry and deployment manifest. A host Unicode implementation may be used only when startup and CI conformance fixtures establish the pinned results for every supported code-point class; otherwise the application uses bundled pinned tables. An unknown host/table mismatch blocks canonical filename normalization and package activation. Runtime upgrades do not silently change canonical identities; runtime or browser Unicode behavior may not silently redefine canonical identity. Every set-valued array has one named versioned normalizer. Every contentSha256, recordSha256, project hash, package hash, proof hash, scope hash, and terminal hash has a closed JSON-pointer inclusion and omission set registered in workflow-schema.js. No implementation selects preimage fields implicitly.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The controlling normative source is the exact UTF-8 file `specification/closed-loop-reliability-controlling-implementation-specification.txt` in the exact audited source commit. CI MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-specification-manifest.json` as a repository-only closed-loop-specification-manifest/1 after reading those exact bytes and MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-normative-requirements.json` as the corresponding normative-requirement manifest. That manifest records the source commit, repository path, artifact filename, byte length, SHA-256, section inventory, contract-profile identity, and the identity and digest of the normative-requirement manifest. The manifest and source commit together identify the exact specification used for implementation and acceptance; the specification does not contain a self-referential digest of itself.

Repository governance MUST maintain one machine-readable closed-loop-normative-requirements/1 manifest generated from and reviewed against the controlling specification. It assigns a stable NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT_ID to every distinct normative requirement, prohibition, invariant, field contract, operation contract, negative case, regression obligation, deployment obligation, and definition-of-done metric. Each entry records the controlling text location, responsible implementation owner, schema or registry entry, deterministic and semantic test IDs, mutation-test IDs, required browser or physical-device proof, acceptance-report field, and current disposition.

14.5 Authoritative field registry
An unregistered field, multiply classified field, ambiguous producer, undeclared default, or operation writing outside its declared set is invalid.

Registry completeness is specification-controlled, not implementation-chosen. Every field named anywhere in this specification receives its complete FIELD_REGISTRY contract either from an explicit statement of this specification or from these closed default rules, applied in order:
1. a field defined in Section 15 uses its Section 15 row and the Section 15 value contracts;
2. STAGE_DECISION, DECISION_EVIDENCE, and every *_DETERMINATION, CONTROLLING_REASON, CONTROLLING_EVIDENCE, and FINAL_* field is an APPLICATION-derived gate summary;

3. every count, coverage, or completeness field — including TOTAL_*, *_COVERAGE, ALL_*, EXPECTED_*, ACTUAL_*, MISSING_*, EXECUTED, SATISFIED, VIOLATED, UNDETERMINED, and RUNS — is an APPLICATION-derived summary under Sections 14.1 and 16.2;
4. every *_RECORDS field is a Section 14.8 projection of its owning Section 38 family, and substantive ownership follows that family's declared partitions;
5. every *_VERSION and *_ID field is an APPLICATION-allocated identity under Section 34.2 or its owning version registry;
6. fields assigned by Sections 14.2, 14.3, and 14.6 follow those assignments;

7. every remaining stage field is an APPLICATION-recomputed summary or immutable reference under Section 14.8; substantive agent or human content never exists as a bare stage field and lives only in its owning family.

A field whose contract is neither explicitly specified nor uniquely produced by these rules is UNDEFINED_FIELD_CONTRACT and blocks specification acceptance; the resolution is a specification change, never an implementation choice.

Canonical record families are the sole substantive authority. A stage field that concerns canonical data is exactly one of:
- an agent proposal before acceptance;
- an immutable ID reference to canonical records;

- audit-only historical data that cannot gate.

Canonical record families are the sole substantive authority. A stage field that concerns canonical data is exactly one of:
- an agent proposal before acceptance;
- an immutable ID reference to canonical records;
- an application-recomputed summary derived exclusively from canonical records;
- audit-only historical data that cannot gate.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.
14.7 Stage-operation scope matrix
Every operation binds jobId, stage, operation, expected projectRevision, contractProfileId, prompt or command identity, and scopeHash. Additional required scope is:

Each matrix entry is statically classified as INPUT_CURRENT, TARGET_RESERVED, or IMMUTABLE_REFERENCE by STAGE_OPERATION_SCOPE_MATRIX. Creation operations use application-reserved target identities for the version or record they create; they do not pretend that the target already exists. Read dependencies use current input identities. The response echoes both classes in their registered locations, and the application verifies every input current and every target still reserved.

A dimension designated by this matrix is required and non-null. A scope dimension not designated for the operation is prohibited unless the registry marks it as an immutable referenced target. Missing, extra, stale, unreserved, or inconsistent dimensions are rejected before proposal creation or command execution.

26.1 Stage 11
Application-established conditions include:
- exactly one current context per run;
- all ten context IDs are distinct;
- all supplied external context identifiers are distinct;
- every run uses the same current candidate ID;
- every run uses the same candidate component hashes;
- no context is linked to another run;
- no prior-run output appears in authorized inputs;
- no reviewer feedback appears in authorized inputs;
- no failure explanation appears in authorized inputs;
- no proposed correction appears in authorized inputs;
- contamination is not affirmative;
- context records are current-scope;
- superseded or failed-attempt contexts are historical and excluded from the distinctness set.
26.2 Stage 12
Conditions include:
- verifier context differs from generator context;
- verifier context is not an impermissible generator context;
- verifier context is current;
- verifier receives only the allowed verification projection;
- verifier does not receive another verifier's conclusion;
- verifier does not receive Stage 13 comparison;
- verifier does not receive RCA;
- verifier does not receive correction proposals.
26.3 Stages 23 and 24
Conditions include:
- reviewer context differs from Stage 21 production context;
- prior reviewer conclusions are withheld unless explicitly necessary;
- generator reasoning is withheld;
- generator self-evaluation is withheld;
- Stage 24 receives only authorized historical failure or regression patterns.
26.4 Gate consequence
Where independence is mandatory:
- APPLICATION_ESTABLISHED → acceptable;
- sufficiently evidenced EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED → potentially acceptable;
- SELF_ASSERTED → insufficient where application evidence should exist;
- UNKNOWN → blocked or undetermined;
- VIOLATED → failure.
The application preserves epistemic limits.
It does not call unobservable external separation application-proven.
Agent statements of independence are corroborating evidence only.
They cannot override reused context identities.
26.5 Independent semantic-review contract
Every release-bearing semantic review records:
- reviewed proposal or record IDs and hashes;
- author context and operation reservation;
- reviewer context and operation reservation;
- required independence dimensions and actual bases;
- review question and allowed dispositions;
- observation and evidence IDs;
- result: ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PARTIAL, UNKNOWN, or DISAGREED;
- reconciliation requirement and status.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.
26.6 Dimensioned independence

Independence is recorded separately for APPLICATION_SESSION_DISTINCTNESS, APPLICATION_INPUT_ISOLATION, USER_TRANSFER_CONFORMITY, EXTERNAL_CONTEXT_IDENTIFIER_DISTINCTNESS, PROVIDER_CONTEXT_INDEPENDENCE, EXECUTOR_OR_REVIEWER_ROLE_SEPARATION, and ENVIRONMENT_INDEPENDENCE where required. APPLICATION_ESTABLISHED means only that application-observable dimensions required by the contract are satisfied. Distinct IDs do not prove hidden provider-state independence. A required UNKNOWN dimension blocks or leaves the result undetermined.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 2.2 Normative-requirement manifest

Repository governance MUST maintain one machine-readable closed-loop-normative-requirements/1 manifest generated from and reviewed against the controlling specification. It assigns a stable NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT_ID to every distinct normative requirement, prohibition, invariant, field contract, operation contract, negative case, regression obligation, deployment obligation, and definition-of-done metric. Each entry records the controlling text location, responsible implementation owner, schema or registry entry, deterministic and semantic test IDs, mutation-test IDs, required browser or physical-device proof, acceptance-report field, and current disposition.

This manifest is implementation and acceptance evidence outside runtime project state. It MUST NOT be injected into ordinary project prompts or carried by the application as project content. CI rejects missing, duplicated, untraced, or conflicting normative entries and rejects an acceptance claim when any current mandatory entry lacks the required implementation and proof relationships.

Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content. One extractor drafts the manifest from the controlling text; an independent reviewer that did not receive the draft performs its own extraction or section-by-section coverage pass; a distinct reconciliation resolves every difference; and every specification section is either covered by entries or explicitly recorded as nonnormative with a reason. CI records the challenge and reconciliation evidence with the manifest digest. An unreconciled material disagreement, an uncovered section, or a missing challenge record blocks acceptance.

The same closure governs STAGE_OPERATION_REGISTRY. For every operation: executor class, response permissions, and writable-family constraints come from Section 14.6; required scope from Section 14.7; acceptance mode from Section 17.12; writable families are exactly the Section 38 families whose records the operation's Section 37 description and Section 14.6 contract create or complete, and the Stage 17 and Stage 19 iteration operations reuse the families of their corresponding Stage 10-16 and Stage 15 operations under the new iteration scope; the completion predicate is the owning stage's Section 37 Completion clause; retry behavior is Section 35.6 for exact retries and replacement-prompt regeneration otherwise; independence requirements are exactly those Sections 26.1-26.6 impose on the operation's role. contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 14.6 Closed stage-operation registry
The exact stage-operation set is:

No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.
Operation execution and response permissions are closed:

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.

- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.

- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation: executor class, response permissions, and writable-family constraints come from Section 14.6; required scope from Section 14.7; acceptance mode from Section 17.12; writable families are exactly the Section 38 families whose records the operation's Section 37 description and Section 14.6 contract create or complete, and the Stage 17 and Stage 19 iteration operations reuse the families of their corresponding Stage 10-16 and Stage 15 operations under the new iteration scope; the completion predicate is the owning stage's Section 37 Completion clause; retry behavior is Section 35.6 for exact retries and replacement-prompt regeneration otherwise; independence requirements are exactly those Sections 26.1-26.6 impose on the operation's role. A stage-operation property neither fixed by this specification nor uniquely derivable from these rules is UNDEFINED_OPERATION_CONTRACT and blocks acceptance.
14.6 Closed stage-operation registry
The exact stage-operation set is:
Operation execution and response permissions are closed:

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.

- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.

- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.
14.7 Stage-operation scope matrix
Every operation binds jobId, stage, operation, expected projectRevision, contractProfileId, prompt or command identity, and scopeHash. Additional required scope is:

Each matrix entry is statically classified as INPUT_CURRENT, TARGET_RESERVED, or IMMUTABLE_REFERENCE by STAGE_OPERATION_SCOPE_MATRIX. Creation operations use application-reserved target identities for the version or record they create; they do not pretend that the target already exists. Read dependencies use current input identities. The response echoes both classes in their registered locations, and the application verifies every input current and every target still reserved.

A dimension designated by this matrix is required and non-null. A scope dimension not designated for the operation is prohibited unless the registry marks it as an immutable referenced target. Missing, extra, stale, unreserved, or inconsistent dimensions are rejected before proposal creation or command execution.

- UTF-8 without BOM;
- rejection of duplicate object names and unpaired surrogates;
- safe-integer-only JSON numbers, with typed canonical strings for other exact numbers;

- exact preservation of array order unless the owning schema declares a named set normalizer;
- exact string scalar values and line endings;

- no escaping of printable non-ASCII scalar values;
- rejection of negative zero, NaN, Infinity, undefined, sparse holes, cyclic values, and implementation objects.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 14.7 Stage-operation scope matrix
Every operation binds jobId, stage, operation, expected projectRevision, contractProfileId, prompt or command identity, and scopeHash. Additional required scope is:

Each matrix entry is statically classified as INPUT_CURRENT, TARGET_RESERVED, or IMMUTABLE_REFERENCE by STAGE_OPERATION_SCOPE_MATRIX. Creation operations use application-reserved target identities for the version or record they create; they do not pretend that the target already exists. Read dependencies use current input identities. The response echoes both classes in their registered locations, and the application verifies every input current and every target still reserved.

A dimension designated by this matrix is required and non-null. A scope dimension not designated for the operation is prohibited unless the registry marks it as an immutable referenced target. Missing, extra, stale, unreserved, or inconsistent dimensions are rejected before proposal creation or command execution.

The DURABLE_OBJECT_REGISTRY declares identity, parent family if nested, producer partitions, lifecycle policy, scope, relationships, hash inclusion set, migration behavior, and gate use. No release-bearing search contract, challenge, semantic review, human decision, disclosure authorization, proof obligation, observation, entailment review, expected-variance contract, environment manifest, capability record, backup record, materiality review, derivation record, operation reservation, delivery candidate, delivery record, or delivery-attempt record may exist only as an untyped stageData blob.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The controlling disposition for every gate, stage determination, release determination, and terminal determination is evaluated in this exact order:
1.1 Any current sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition -> REJECTED.
1.2 Otherwise any required unknown, insufficiency, contradiction, stale state, unresolved blocker, or unavailable mandatory capability -> BLOCKED.
1.3 Otherwise every applicable mandatory proposition satisfied -> ACCEPTED.
1.4 All blockers and contradictions remain recorded even when REJECTED controls the disposition.
Within its declared support contract, the application MUST guarantee:
- REJECTED
- BLOCKED
- UNDETERMINED
- EXECUTION_FAILED
- HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED

requirements.controllingText: The external agent may ask concise human-authority questions in the external conversation. A human-origin answer first supplied there remains an EXTERNAL_CLAIM until the agent returns it in the response JSON and the application presents the exact extracted answer for one-action confirmation or correction. The resulting confirmation creates the HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION record and provenance link. Exact confirmation may be atomically co-accepted with the dependent proposal under Section 14.10; correction requires a replacement prompt. The operator is not required to retype the answer. Facts already present in current raw input or accepted human records are not reconfirmed.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 6.4A External-conversation human-answer capture
14.10 Human-origin facts first supplied during an external conversation

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

unresolvedAmbiguities.statement: Section 1 gives REJECTED precedence for sufficient mandatory refutation; 29.15 line 2594 says that such refutation blocks release regardless of severity. Preserve the difference between disallowing release and disposition label; do not silently reinterpret this as BLOCKED.
The exact Stage 17/19 family correspondence must be checked against complete Sections 37 and 38 before accepting these scopes.
All fields named anywhere in Sections 0–52 remain to be checked against explicit and ordered default contracts; no implementation-selected field contract is inferred.

Actual per-operation INPUT_CURRENT/TARGET_RESERVED/IMMUTABLE_REFERENCE classification must be checked against the remaining stage and owning-family contracts. Current draft scopes preserve the matrix condition without inventing that classification.

Repeated source-native requirements and general guarantees are retained as candidate scopes at each source anchor. They are not counted as distinct accepted obligations until proposition-equivalence review resolves repetition versus additional scope.

Sequences, closed enums, quantified target sets, and alternative outcomes are retained when they form one candidate acceptance predicate; independent review must still challenge their atomic boundaries. Punctuation or covered bytes was not treated as atomicity proof.
The unread remainder may add controlling conditions, exceptions, negative tests, metrics, or definitions to already drafted propositions. All draft rows remain context-review-pending.

limitations: Draft propositions are candidate semantic scopes, not accepted authoritative requirements or implementation proof.
No historical ID crosswalk is asserted; old-ID retention needs separate reviewed reconciliation.
Whole-line primary spans deliberately retain shared subjects and qualifiers; their overlap is not completeness evidence.
Cross-section context must be completed before any row is treated as reconciled.
Unread and unextracted ranges remain normative-unknown, never nonnormative.
The scope serialization follows the read source §34.1 for the draft value domain; no comparison with repository implementation has been performed.
Candidate primary line coverage and candidate counts are navigation checks, never proof of distinct-obligation completeness.
